title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from the cote and the last line): an elliptic curve in characteristic ≠ 2 in Weierstrass form y^2 = c(x-ξ1)(x-ξ2)(x-ξ3), with the ξ_i distinct. The ξ_i = ℘(ε_i) are the x-coordinates (℘-values) of the three nonzero 2-torsion points ε_i. So the curve comes with a level-2 structure. The e_i form a basis indexed by the 2-torsion points; their exact meaning (formal basis, basis of a module of functions, or dual basis of evaluations) is not specified on this page.

On the previous page Grothendieck sets up a 2x2 linear problem for unknown vectors f1, f2: ξ_i f1 + f2 = (e_j - e_k)/(ξ_j - ξ_k) for (i,j,k) a cyclic permutation of (1,2,3). Equivalently, the affine-linear vector function x ↦ x f1 + f2 is prescribed at the three points ξ_i. This is a Lagrange/Vandermonde-type interpolation, and the system is consistent.

He solves it by brute force on the previous page. Here he records the result in symmetric form. Put Δ0 = (ξ1-ξ2)(ξ2-ξ3)(ξ3-ξ1), a square root of the discriminant up to a constant (disc ∝ Δ0^2). Then:
- Δ0 f1 = Σ_cyc (ξ_j - ξ_k) e_i
- -Δ0 f2 = Σ_cyc ξ_i (ξ_j - ξ_k) e_i

He concludes that a certain element t (probably a tangent or deformation vector on the level-2 moduli, or a distinguished vector in the 2-dimensional representation of S_3 ≅ GL_2(F_2)) corresponds, up to the factor Δ0, to Σ_cyc (ξ_j - ξ_k) e_i = Σ_i (℘(ε_j) - ℘(ε_k)) e_i. The aim is to express this vector intrinsically through the 2-torsion points and the ℘-function. The construction is part of a level-2 (Legendre-type) description of the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2.
errors: No errors. Check: substituting the boxed formulas gives ξ1 f1 + f2 = (1/Δ0) Σ_i (ξ1 - ξ_i)(ξ_j - ξ_k) e_i. The e1-coefficient is 0. The e2-coefficient is (ξ1-ξ2)(ξ3-ξ1)/Δ0 = 1/(ξ2-ξ3). The e3-coefficient is (ξ1-ξ3)(ξ1-ξ2)/Δ0 = -1/(ξ2-ξ3). This agrees with the system; the other two equations follow by cyclic symmetry.
Minor: the meaning of 't' and of the e_i is not stated on this page, so the final identification cannot be fully verified from it alone.

ideas.what: Solving the interpolation system ξ_i f1 + f2 = (e_j - e_k)/(ξ_j - ξ_k) in closed form using the Vandermonde-type product Δ0 = ∏(ξ_i - ξ_j) (cyclic)
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange interpolation / inverse of a Vandermonde matrix; square root of the discriminant

ideas.what: Expressing a vector attached to the curve as Σ_i (℘(ε_j) - ℘(ε_k)) e_i, indexed by the 2-torsion points ε_i
ideas.modern_name: level-2 structure; differences of 2-division values e_j - e_k (related to fourth powers of theta constants); the S_3 = GL_2(F_2) action on the 2-torsion
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Weierstrass, Jacobi, Legendre); in moduli terms Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, correct linear-algebra computation (Vandermonde/Lagrange inversion) in the classical level-2 Weierstrass setting. It is a scratch step within notes on the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, with no new construction or connection visible on this page.
